claim: No board in section 18 draws the panel body for an APPROVED round; 158:213 claimed the panel was gone instead.
truth: ReviewTab has no APPROVED branch at all. Its body chain is revoked -> changes_requested -> total===0 -> openComments===0 -> null. An APPROVED round with zero comments therefore falls into `emptyBody` and tells the designer 'Sara has not commented yet. You will be notified.' — after the client has already approved. An APPROVED round whose comments are all resolved falls into `allResolvedBody`, which says 'Everything is resolved… ready to send round N+1' and still never says approved.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/sidebar/tabs/review/ReviewTab.tsx:681-689 — the ternary chain is `round.revoked ? revokedBody : round.status?.toLowerCase() === "changes_requested" ? changesRequestedBody : total === 0 ? emptyBody : openComments.length === 0 ? allResolvedBody : null`; there is no `=== "approved"` test in the file. :629-636 emptyBody renders 'has not commented yet. / You will be notified.'. :602-609 allResolvedBody. Contrast :615-626 changesRequestedBody, which exists precisely because the same bug was fixed for CHANGES_REQUESTED (see its comment at :611-614).

claim: 157:221 draws the reassurance 'You will be notified.' under 'Sara has not commented yet.'
truth: Nobody is notified. No review or comment event creates a Notification row or sends any email to the designer. When the client approves or asks for changes through their token link, the write happens and nothing else fires — no notification, no mail. The designer learns about it only by opening the editor, which re-reads the round on mount. The only emails in the whole loop go the other way (to admins and to the client, at submit time).

claim: caption/Review panel · re-sending (161:8) captions 158:57 'Review panel · re-sending' as a single, uniform re-send.
truth: There are two Re-send buttons in the product on two different code paths, and only one of them works. The Review panel passes the round's invitedEmail forward; the ReviewBar strip under the topbar calls the same handler with NO argument. submitReview mints a token only when given an email, and opening a new round revokes every earlier token for the site. So re-sending a CHANGES_REQUESTED round from the ReviewBar creates a new round, kills the client's live link, and mints no replacement — the client is locked out with no link at all.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/sidebar/tabs/review/ReviewTab.tsx:295 `const outcome = await onResend(round?.invitedEmail ?? undefined);` (correct). packages/editor/src/editor/shell/ReviewBar.tsx:108 `await onResend();` — no argument. Both are wired to the same handler: AquibraStudio.tsx:536 `onResend={resendReview}` for the bar and :584 `onResendReview={resendReview}` for the panel; resendReview is defined at :401-421 and forwards clientEmail to submitForReview. server/services/review.service.ts:93-95 `if (clientEmail) { ({ token } = await issueReviewToken(request.id, clientEmail)); }` — no email, no token. :59-66 a non-PENDING round takes the create branch, setting openedNewRound = true; :104-109 then `prisma.reviewRequest.updateMany({ where: { siteId, id: { not: request.id }, token: { not: null }, revokedAt: null }, data: { revokedAt: new Date() } })`. ReviewBar renders for CHANGES_REQUESTED (ReviewBar.tsx:50).
edit: Node 161:8: extend the caption to name the split. Append: 'Two Re-send paths exist. The panel passes the round's invitedEmail (ReviewTab.tsx:295); the ReviewBar strip calls the same handler with no argument (ReviewBar.tsx:108), which on a CHANGES_REQUESTED round opens a new round, revokes the client's live token (review.service.ts:104-109) and mints no replacement. The board draws the panel path.' Resize the caption to 280x90.

ReviewTab.tsx:250 `await postReply(body, activePage)` where activePage is :242 `comments[0]?.pageId`.

claim: Every comment row on every board is attributed either to the client by name ('Sara · client · Home · 2d') or, for internal rows, implicitly.
truth: Internal comments are always labelled 'You', whoever wrote them. The panel resolves a name only for CLIENT comments (via the reviewer join); authorId is never resolved to a user name anywhere, and Comment declares no relation to User for that column. So on a two-designer team every teammate's note reads as your own. A comment whose external author was deleted also degrades: reviewerId is ON DELETE SET NULL, which turns a client comment into an internal one and relabels it 'You'.

"Client") : "You"}`. packages/editor/src/services/ReviewService.ts:195-196 `authorKind: r.reviewerId ? "client" : "internal", authorName: r.reviewer?.name ?? null` — authorName is populated only from the reviewer join. server/services/comment.service.ts:49-53 listComments includes `reviewer: { select: { name: true } }` and nothing for authorId; :56-67 resolves names for resolvedById only. prisma/schema.prisma:491-492 — Comment relates to Site and Reviewer only; there is no author User relation, and `reviewer … onDelete: SetNull` at :492 is what flips a deleted reviewer's comment to internal.

: null}`.

claim: Canonical page 1:6 draws 'S5.5 · load-error' as a state distinct from the dead-link screens.
truth: The client page cannot produce a load-error. Every failure of the token query — including a genuine network or server failure that carries no domain reason — falls through the same lookup and defaults to the NOT_FOUND copy, so a transport failure tells the client 'This link doesn't work / It may have been copied incompletely. Try clicking the link in your email again rather than pasting it.' There is no retry and no distinct error screen. The state the board draws is unreachable; the underlying behaviour is a real defect, but it is not this board.
evidence: packages/dashboard/app/review/[token]/review-client.tsx:159-176 — `if (review.error) { const reason = (review.error.data?.cause as {reason?:string}|undefined)?.reason; const code = review.error.data?.code ?? "NOT_FOUND"; const copy = DEAD_LINK_COPY[reason ?? ""] ?? DEAD_LINK_COPY[code] ?? DEAD_LINK_COPY.NOT_FOUND; …}`. DEAD_LINK_COPY (:16-33) has only EXPIRED, REVOKED, NOT_FOUND and CONFLICT keys — no INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR/TIMEOUT — so any other code lands on NOT_FOUND. The query is `{ retry: false }` at :126, and no branch renders a retry control.
edit: Rename 121:25 to 'NOT IMPLEMENTED — a transport failure renders the not-found dead-link copy; there is no load-error screen and no retry' and add the note to its caption 122:64. Do NOT delete the frame — it is the design for a state the product should have.

claim: 1339:7221 'Client sign-off · F · dead-link · conflict' carries an inline 'UNBUILDABLE' suffix, which is not the marker convention used elsewhere in the file.

The page's CONFLICT copy ('You've already answered this') is dead code: the only error the loader can raise is INVALID_TOKEN, REVOKED or EXPIRED, and CONFLICT is produced solely by the resolve mutation — whose error object is never rendered anywhere on the page.

ALREADY_RESOLVED is thrown only by resolveReviewByToken at :278-280. server/trpc/routers/client-review.ts:50-52 maps ALREADY_RESOLVED to CONFLICT. In packages/dashboard/app/review/[token]/review-client.tsx the rendered error objects are identify.error (:230-232) and comment.error (:353-355, :390-396) only — `resolve.error` appears nowhere in the file; resolve is read only for isPending (:292, :299, :447, :451, :456). So DEAD_LINK_COPY.CONFLICT at :29-32 is unreachable.

claim: 'Client sign-off · E · post-approval-edited' draws the returning client being told the designer has made changes since they approved.
truth: The state is real and reachable, but only by SOME edits, and the board implies any change triggers it. Staleness is a single timestamp comparison against site.lastEditedAt. That column is stamped by the editor's project save, site create/rename/duplicate, theme writes, template application and the AI generation worker — and by nothing in the CMS, page, media or component-library services. So a client can approve, the team can rewrite every CMS record, add and delete pages, swap every image and edit saved components, and this board never appears: the approval keeps reading current.
evidence: packages/dashboard/app/review/[token]/review-client.tsx:260 gates on data.editedSinceApproval, computed at server/services/client-review.service.ts:168-172 `review.status === "APPROVED" && review.resolvedAt !== null && review.site.lastEditedAt !== null && review.site.lastEditedAt.getTime() > review.resolvedAt.getTime()`. Writers of lastEditedAt across server/, packages/dashboard/, packages/shared/, packages/editor/src/ and lib/ (exhaustive grep, node_modules/.next excluded): sites.service.ts:196, 225, 315, 380, 741; theme.service.ts:186, 274; template.service.ts:162, 221; packages/dashboard/app/api/workers/ai-generate/[jobId]/route.ts:194, 207. The grep returns NO line in cms.service.ts, page.service.ts, media.service.ts or site-component.service.ts — page.service.ts writes prisma.page.create/update/delete at :77, :105, :124, :211, :231 with no site update. Prior finding MOD-A-08 (docs/design-jobs/findings/MOD-A.jsonl) measured the CMS half of this independently.
edit: Append to the name of 1340:7174: '— reachable only via canvas save, rename, duplicate, theme or template writes (sites.service.ts:741,315,380; theme.service.ts:186,274). CMS record edits, page create/update/delete, media and component-library changes do NOT stamp site.lastEditedAt, so they never make an approval stale (cf. MOD-A-08).' Consider a companion board 'Client sign-off · E · NOT reached after CMS edit' only if the coordinator wants the negative drawn.

claim: Canonical page 1:6 draws 'S5.5 · brand-colour' (125:2) and 'S5.5 · brand-colour-fails-contrast' (125:49), and the page carries a 'Client / Branded bar' component set (2059:7457).
truth: The client review page has no theming of any kind. Every colour is a hardcoded hex literal; there is no accent variable, no workspace brand colour is fetched, and the payload the page receives carries no colour field. The only agency-specific value on the page is the workspace NAME rendered as text. A contrast-failure variant therefore cannot exist either, because there is no configurable colour to fail.

No CSS custom property, no theme prop, no style attribute driven by data. The payload from server/services/client-review.service.ts:141-173 contains reviewId, siteId, siteName, agencyName, status, note, changeSummary, sentAt, snapshotPages, reviewer, editedSinceApproval — no brand or colour field. agencyName is consumed only as text at review-client.tsx:181, :90.
